theorem: For every split Cayley hexagon H(q), the first Betti number of its Levi graph is q^6. Thus beta1(H(4))=4096=|V2| and beta1(H(2))=64. Under the explicit free C13 clock on H(4), the quotient beta1 is 316=1+4095/13, exactly the number of C13 orbits on V2 including zero. Since Phi13 is irreducible over F2 and F2[C13] is semisimple, H1(Levi(H4);F2) and the permutation module F2[V2] restrict isomorphically to C13 as 1^316 + W12^315.
boundary: Exact combinatorial and C13-module theorem. No full G2(4)-module identification is claimed.
